Robust optimization treats uncertain data as an *adversary* that can pick any value from a
given set, and asks for a decision that stays feasible against every such choice. No
probability distribution is needed. The pages here build up to the budget-of-uncertainty
model of @bertsimas2004, which keeps a robust linear program linear and lets the modeller
trade a small loss in the objective for a guaranteed, small probability of constraint
violation.

Compare with [Stochastic Programming](../stochastic-programming/index.qmd), which models
the data with a probability distribution and optimizes an expected value instead.
